name: Operation Paperclip
claim: The US secretly recruited Nazi scientists after World War II.
truth: Over 1,600 German scientists, engineers and technicians were brought to the US, many with Nazi Party or SS membership, their records sanitised to avoid immigration rules. Wernher von Braun, who built the V-2 with slave labour, led NASA's Saturn V programme; Hubertus Strughold, linked to human experiments at Dachau, became a 'father of space medicine'. The USSR ran a similar programme (Operation Osoaviakhim).
evidence: Declassified US government files; the 1998 Nazi War Crimes Disclosure Act released many records.
summary: Verdict: Documented fact. The US secretly recruited Nazi scientists after World War II.

name: Unit 731 and the US cover-up
claim: Japan ran a secret biological-weapons unit that experimented on humans, and its leaders escaped trial.
truth: Unit 731 near Harbin, led by Shirō Ishii, performed vivisections, frostbite tests and deliberate infections with plague, anthrax and cholera on thousands of prisoners, mostly Chinese, and spread plague over Chinese cities, killing perhaps hundreds of thousands. After the war the US granted Ishii and his staff immunity in exchange for their data; several later held prominent medical posts in Japan.
evidence: Testimony at the Soviet Khabarovsk trials (1949); declassified US documents; Japanese researchers' confessions in the 1990s.
summary: Verdict: Documented fact. Japan ran a secret biological-weapons unit that experimented on humans, and its leaders escaped trial.

name: MKUltra
claim: The CIA secretly drugged people with LSD in mind-control experiments.
truth: Under MKUltra, the CIA funded experiments at universities, hospitals and prisons, giving LSD and other drugs to people, sometimes without consent, and testing hypnosis and sensory deprivation; in Montreal, psychiatrist Ewen Cameron 'depatterned' patients with electroshock. CIA director Richard Helms ordered most files destroyed in 1973.
evidence: The 1975 Church Committee and 1977 Senate hearings, based on 20,000 surviving documents found in financial records.

name: Tuskegee syphilis study
claim: US health officials deliberately left Black men with syphilis untreated to study the disease.
truth: The US Public Health Service followed about 600 poor Black men, 399 with syphilis, telling them they were treated for 'bad blood'. Even after penicillin became the standard cure in 1947, they were denied treatment. Dozens died and wives and children were infected. A whistle-blower, Peter Buxtun, leaked it to the press in 1972. President Clinton apologised in 1997. A related US study deliberately infected Guatemalans in 1946–48.

name: Gulf of Tonkin incident
claim: The second North Vietnamese attack used to justify US war in Vietnam never happened.
truth: On 2 August 1964 North Vietnamese boats did attack the USS Maddox. But the reported second attack on 4 August almost certainly did not occur — sonar and radar misreadings in a storm. President Johnson used it to pass the Gulf of Tonkin Resolution, escalating the Vietnam War, in which over 3 million people died.
evidence: NSA historian Robert Hanyok's study, declassified in 2005.

name: Radium Girls
claim: Companies knew radium paint was poisoning women workers and hid it.
truth: Young women painting watch dials with glow-in-the-dark radium paint were told to lick their brushes to a point. Many developed bone decay ('radium jaw'), anaemia and cancer. Company executives handled radium with protection, while doctors hired by companies blamed syphilis. The women's lawsuits (1928) helped establish workplace safety laws.
evidence: Court records; Kate Moore's history The Radium Girls.

name: Leaded petrol cover-up
claim: The industry promoted leaded petrol despite knowing lead was poisonous.
truth: General Motors chemist Thomas Midgley developed tetraethyl lead in 1921; workers at plants died of lead poisoning, and Midgley himself was poisoned. Industry-funded scientist Robert Kehoe claimed for decades it was safe, until Clair Patterson's research proved widespread lead pollution. Lead exposure lowered IQ of hundreds of millions of children. The last country stopped selling it in 2021.

claim: Churchill's government made the Bengal famine worse.

evidence: War cabinet records; Madhusree Mukerjee, Churchill's Secret War (2010); debates among historians.

name: Death of Subhas Chandra Bose
claim: Bose did not die in the 1945 plane crash.

link_text: Union Carbide ignored safety warnings and its chairman escaped trial. Safety systems were off or broken; earlier leaks had been reported. Chairman Warren Anderson was arrested, released on bail, flew out of India and never returned. A 1989 settlement of $470 million was criticised as too low. Court records; investigations. Bhopal, India
